question: Which of the following revolutionists was associated with the Anushilan Samiti?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jatindra Mohan Sengupta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Jatindra Mohan Sengupta was a prominent leader associated with the Anushilan Samiti.
 
• He was involved in the** Non-Cooperation Movement and the Civil Disobedience Movement.**
 
• Sengupta was also a** member of the Indian National Congress** and worked closely with other prominent leaders like Subhas Chandra Bose.
 
• The Anushilan Samiti was a revolutionary group that played a significant role in the Indian independence struggle.
 
• The Anushilan Samiti was** founded in 1902 **and had two main branches: the **Jugantar group in Kolkata and the Dhaka Anushilan Samiti.**
 
• Key figures in the Anushilan Samiti included Aurobindo Ghosh, Barindra Kumar Ghosh, and Rash Behari Bose.
 
• The Samiti was involved in several notable revolutionary activities, including the Alipore Bomb Case and the attempt on the life of the Viceroy of India in 1912.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhagat Singh**, **Rajguru**, and **Sukhdev** were associated with the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA), not the Anushilan Samiti.

**Hindustan Republican Association (HRA):**

 
• Formation:** Established in 1924** by revolutionaries like **Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan, Sachindra Nath Bakshi, and Sachindranath Sanyal**.
 
• Objective: To achieve complete independence from British rule through armed revolution.
 
• Key Activities: Known for the** Kakori Train Robbery in 1925**, where they looted a train carrying British government funds.
 
• Ideology: Initially focused on establishing a Federated Republic of the United States of India**.**

**Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA):**

 
• Formation: Renamed from HRA to HSRA in** 1928** to include socialist principles.
 
• Key Leaders:** Bhagat Singh, Chandrashekhar Azad, Sukhdev, and others.**
 
• Objective: To overthrow British rule and establish a** socialist republic in India.**
 
• Key Activities: Involved in several revolutionary activities, including the assassination of British police officer J.P. Saunders to avenge the death of Lala Lajpat Rai.
 
• Ideology: Emphasized socialism and aimed to abolish exploitation of man by man.
